claim: Risk = uncertainty of outcome, mainly the chance of loss; banks manage risk, they cannot remove it
source: concept

claim: RBI: banks face financial and non-financial risks (credit, interest rate, FX, liquidity, equity, commodity, legal, regulatory, reputational, operational); risks are interdependent
source: RBI Risk Management Systems in Banks (guidance note 1999)

claim: Expected loss = average expected losses, a cost of business managed through pricing and provisioning; unexpected loss = losses above expected, covered by capital (loss-absorbing)
source: BCBS Explanatory Note on the Basel II IRB Risk Weight Functions

claim: RAROC compares businesses of different risk; capital allocated rises with volatility of returns; hurdle rate sets target pricing
source: RBI Guidance Note on Credit Risk Management

claim: Identify, measure, monitor and control the overall level of risks
source: RBI Risk Management Systems in Banks

claim: Credit risk = inability or unwillingness of a customer or counterparty to meet commitments in lending, trading, hedging, settlement and other transactions; transaction (default) risk and portfolio risk (intrinsic, concentration)
source: RBI Risk Management Systems in Banks

claim: Credit losses also from reduction in portfolio value due to actual or perceived deterioration in credit quality (downgrade without default)
source: RBI Guidance Note on Credit Risk Management

claim: Counterparty credit risk = counterparty could default before final settlement; bilateral risk of loss
source: Basel Framework

claim: FX principal (settlement) risk: pay the currency sold, fail to receive the currency bought; full value at risk; called Herstatt risk; Bankhaus Herstatt failed 1974
source: BCBS Supervisory guidance on FX settlement risk

claim: Country risk = country unable to service debts to foreign lenders in time; transfer risk is the core (can pay locally, not in FCY); sovereign risk = lending to a government or on its guarantee
source: RBI Guidance Note on Credit Risk Management

claim: Market risk = risk of losses in on- and off-balance sheet positions from movements in market prices
source: Basel Framework

claim: Market variables: interest rate, FX rate, equity price, commodity price
source: RBI Risk Management Systems in Banks

claim: Liquidity risk from funding long-term assets with short-term liabilities (rollover); funding risk (deposits withdrawn / not renewed), time risk (expected inflows not received, NPAs), call risk (contingent liabilities crystallise; missed business opportunities)
source: RBI Risk Management Systems in Banks

claim: Interest rate risk = impact of unexpected rate changes on NII / NIM or market value of equity
source: RBI Risk Management Systems in Banks; RBI ALM circular

claim: IRR types: gap/mismatch (different amounts, maturity or repricing dates), basis (rates change by different magnitudes; high in Indian loan books; can be favourable), embedded option (prepayment, premature withdrawal), yield curve (non-parallel moves), price (sale before maturity; trading book), reinvestment (rate on future cash flows), net interest position (more earning assets than paying liabilities; float a natural hedge)
source: RBI Risk Management Systems in Banks

claim: Operational risk = loss from inadequate or failed internal processes, people and systems or from external events; includes legal risk; excludes strategic and reputational risk
source: Basel Framework

claim: Older RBI wording: operational risk = any risk not categorised as market or credit risk, or loss from human or technical error
source: RBI Risk Management Systems in Banks

claim: Compliance risk = risk of legal or regulatory sanctions, material financial loss or loss to reputation from failure to comply with laws, regulations, rules, SRO standards and codes of conduct
source: BCBS Compliance and the compliance function in banks

claim: Reputational risk = negative perception by customers, counterparties, shareholders, investors, analysts, regulators etc. that hurts business relationships and access to funding; can lead to credit, liquidity, market and legal risk; addressed in ICAAP
source: BCBS Enhancements to the Basel II framework

claim: Strategic risk = loss from wrong business decisions or poor implementation
source: concept

claim: Systemic risk = failure of one institution spreads (contagion) to the system
source: concept

claim: Model risk = adverse outcomes of a model from errors, misapplication, unsuitability over time
source: RBI draft Guidance on Regulatory Principles for Model Risk Management 2026
status: verified as draft; freeze: check if finalised

claim: Physical risk (acute: floods, heatwaves, storms; chronic: gradual shifts, rising seas and temperatures); transition risk (climate policy and regulation, new technology, customer preferences)
source: RBI draft Disclosure framework on Climate-related Financial Risks 2024
status: verified as draft; freeze: status of final rules

claim: Trading book = instruments held for short-term resale, short-term price profit, arbitrage, or hedging these; banking book = all other instruments
source: Basel Framework

claim: Investments classified HTM, AFS, FVTPL; HFT a separate sub-category within FVTPL; category decided at or before acquisition
source: RBI Investment Portfolio Directions 2025

claim: HTM: hold to collect contractual cash flows, SPPI; carried at cost, not marked to market
source: RBI Investment Portfolio Directions 2025

claim: AFS: collect cash flows and sell, SPPI; fair valued at least quarterly; net gains/losses to AFS-Reserve, not P&L
source: RBI Investment Portfolio Directions 2025

claim: FVTPL: what does not qualify for HTM/AFS (e.g. equity shares, mutual funds); gains/losses to P&L
source: RBI Investment Portfolio Directions 2025

claim: HFT: short-term resale, short-term price profit, arbitrage, hedges of these; fair valued daily through P&L; no legal impediment to sale or hedge
source: RBI Investment Portfolio Directions 2025

claim: IFR discontinued w.e.f. 18 May 2026
source: RBI Investment Portfolio Directions 2025

claim: Trading book for capital = HFT from 1 Apr 2024; HTM, AFS, FVTPL (non-HFT) and investments in own subsidiaries, JVs, associates are banking book and attract no market-risk charge
source: RBI Capital Adequacy Guidelines – Review of Trading Book
status: verified (circular text read; Annex 1 wording via RBI page excerpt; open annex at freeze)

claim: Market Risk Directions 2026 effective 1 Apr 2027; trading book = all HFT instruments; all else banking book with credit-risk or CCR charge
source: RBI Minimum Capital Requirements for Market Risk Directions 2026

claim: Off-balance-sheet items (guarantees, LCs, undrawn limits, derivatives) are contingent and can crystallise; on crystallisation funds may not come from the customer (credit risk) and cash is needed (call risk)
source: RBI Guidance Note on Credit Risk Management; RBI Risk Management Systems
